title: Solving cos(2*theta) + cos(theta) = 0 on [0, 2*pi]
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find all solutions to the equation \cos 2\theta + \cos\theta = 0 in the interval 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.

steps.title: Rewrite cos(2*theta) in Terms of cos(theta) and Factor
steps.explanation: Substitute the double-angle identity cos(2*theta) = 2*cos^2(theta) - 1 to create a quadratic equation in cos(theta), then factor it.
steps.why: Expressing the equation purely in terms of cos(theta) allows standard quadratic factoring.

steps.title: Solve 2*cos(theta) - 1 = 0 on [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Cosine equals 1/2 in Quadrants I and IV at reference angle pi/3, yielding theta = pi/3 and theta = 5*pi/3.

steps.title: Solve cos(theta) + 1 = 0 on [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Cosine equals -1 at the unique angle theta = pi in [0, 2*pi]. Combining all roots gives pi/3, pi, and 5*pi/3.
steps.why: The point (-1, 0) on the unit circle corresponds to theta = pi.
